answer.answer: The coach itinerary is sample planning material, not booking evidence. Passenger-specific airline confirmations establish the booked itinerary: the youth travels ahead through Brussels, the family later meets in Geneva, and all four return together from Milan Linate. Because the return uses Linate rather than Malpensa, the northern-Italy finish remains feasible and planning should preserve a final night in Milan with positioning to Linate.

claims.value: The ski-team packet contains only a coach sample itinerary with example booking references and is not proof of any passenger booking. Passenger-specific airline confirmations reviewed on 2026-07-22 are authoritative and supersede those sample flights.

The confirmed youth outbound is Seattle to Amsterdam to Brussels on August 4-5, 2026, followed by the camp transfer from Brussels to Geneva on August 10, 2026. An official schedule-change notice subsequently moved the August 10 departure 85 minutes earlier without changing its flight number or airports.

The confirmed family outbound is Seattle to London Heathrow to Geneva on August 9-10, 2026. The shared return has all four travelers—including the youth traveler—flying Milan Linate to London Heathrow to Seattle on August 25, 2026.

The confirmed return departs Milan Linate, not Milan Malpensa. This keeps the proposed three- or four-day northern-Italy finish feasible, but the still-unbooked ground itinerary must remain compatible with Linate; the working plan calls for the final night in Milan.

The 2026-07-26 current-status note controls; the 2026-07-23 green checkpoint is historical and explicitly cannot override newer production-sized findings. Connection, authentication, and exact-path reads work, but broad `memory.open` and lexical retrieval are slow and can hit the 30-second database timeout. Retrieval lanes share one transaction, so a later lane failure can also discard an earlier successful lane. Consequently, the current architecture is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth.

Normal writes copy a full corpus membership manifest. With about 64,000 active records and 9.6 million estimated source tokens already in the owner corpus, this full-manifest copying is the identified write-amplification mechanism and contributes to the conclusion that the architecture is not ready at 10x growth.

The approved direction is to make current Markdown files the workspace truth, version only changed files, make indexes and derived views rebuildable, and checkpoint using exact path, version, and hash references plus changes since a workspace generation, while retaining coherent source hydration and compact retrieval packets. This is an approved direction, not evidence of completed implementation.
